question: On the same 50 pinned LeWM PushT dataset tasks, what task-success and synchronized planner-latency changes result from stopping official-teacher CEM after 5, 10, or 20 iterations instead of 30, with candidate and elite counts fixed at 300/30?

scope.evaluation_type: pinned-upstream-protocol-aligned dataset-driven rollout evaluation over the exact 50 selected source tasks
scope.optional_action_difference: omitted; success and synchronized planner timing are the frozen endpoints

protocol.preprocessing: reuse the existing baseline helper: full-dataset StandardScaler for action/proprio/state after NaN-row removal, goal scaler reuse, and pinned ToImage/float32/ImageNet-normalize/Resize(224) transforms
protocol.evaluator: reuse run_dataset_teacher_baseline.evaluate_selected_tasks and the pinned _set_state/_set_goal_state callables; video=None

reference_baseline.engineering_floor: at least 5/50; a continuation gate only
reference_baseline.stage1_rule: Run 300/30/30 first on the exact frozen rows. Require valid finite outcomes for all 50 tasks, at least 5 successes, and itemwise equality to the 25534994 success vector. If any check fails, record the control result and stop before the 5/10/20 arms.

measurement.paired_unit: same selected source task row_index, episode_idx, and start_step; each arm executes the full dataset-driven rollout
measurement.task_success: store the ordered 50-item success vector and report success delta plus both-success/control-only/treatment-only/both-fail pair counts versus the 30-iteration control
measurement.planner_walltime: synchronize CUDA immediately before and after each solver.solve call; retain every solve duration and report total synchronized solve time, call count, and per-solve durations
measurement.steady_state_timing: report median solve duration after the first call and its sample count; report second_solve_seconds separately as descriptive only
measurement.planner_cost: record solver.solve calls and estimated candidate-cost evaluations as iterations * 300 candidates * ceil(n_envs / batch_size) per solve
measurement.changed_actions: each depth arm performs real replanning and environment steps; later states and trajectories may diverge after actions differ
measurement.warm_start: keep pinned PlanConfig warm_start=true; horizon=receding_horizon=5 means the executed plan has no tail to carry into the next solve
measurement.rng_alignment: initialize each arm solver with seed 42; different iteration counts consume different amounts of random state, so task-level candidate innovations are not exactly paired
measurement.primary_comparison: 50-task success-vector and paired outcome counts, plus synchronized solve latency and CEM candidate-cost counts versus 30 iterations
measurement.timing_limit: single seed and fixed arm order; cold-start and order effects are not counterbalanced, so latency results are descriptive
measurement.gpu_telemetry: nvidia-smi utilization and memory every 5 seconds appended to job.log

validity: compute node confirmed by PBS_JOBID and PBS_NODEFILE before heavy imports or model/data I/O
staged LeWM/stable-worldmodel/venv roots match the runner arguments
frozen dataset/checkpoint sizes and job-private cache links match
every arm uses the exact 50 frozen task rows, official teacher, preprocessing, 300 candidates, and top-30 elites
each arm returns 50 finite metrics, 50 finite outcomes, and finite solver actions
the 30-iteration stage-1 success vector exactly matches the reference baseline
validity_and_stopping.stop_after_stage1: stop remaining arms on invalid output, 30-iteration success-vector mismatch, or fewer than 5/50 control successes
validity_and_stopping.no_posthoc_extension: no task substitution, reruns, retuning, extra depths, or additional seeds after inspecting results
validity_and_stopping.inference_limit: single-seed results on 50 paired source tasks are descriptive; no formal noninferiority, random-reset success, or broad generalization claim

compute_node_guards: PBS_NODEFILE is a real file and includes current hostname
resources.login_node_work: control only; no model/data reads, inference, benchmark, download, or heavy I/O
